cases.original_concern: Definition Step 4 says to retain segment labels and their designated endpoints through smoothings, then start each closed component at its least-labelled segment. Smoothing can cut one labelled polygonal segment into multiple surviving pieces, potentially on different components; its original designated endpoints need not remain endpoints of those pieces. No subdivision/relabeling or tie-breaking rule is specified. The claimed deterministic traversal needs this bookkeeping clause; the procedure-properties proof 1.2 assumes it is already determined.

proposals.source_excerpt:
$g_i^{\pm1}T_\mu$. In each current diagram, orient open strands from the smaller to the larger endpoint
   label and order them by their initial endpoints. Order closed components by
   their least segment labels. In each closed component, start by traversing its
   least-labelled segment from its designated initial endpoint to its terminal
   endpoint; then follow the unique continuation of that component, traversing
   later segments in whichever direction reaches the next endpoint. At a crossing
   continue along the same strand, and after a smoothing continue along the
   prescribed pairing. Retain segment labels and their designated endpoints
   through switches and smoothings. This gives a deterministic traversal even
   when segment orientations do not join coherently around a closed component.
proposals.proposed_replacement:
$g_i^{\pm1}T_\mu$. For each initial reducer input (a matrix column here or a
   closed trace diagram in Step 5), first fix pairwise disjoint rational crossing
   boxes, each meeting only its two crossing branches, in four boundary ports,
   and containing no polygonal vertex. Choose the first admissible finite tuple
   in the length-then-lexicographic rational coding order of Step 3. Make the
   boxes small enough that every component contains a segment portion outside
   the boxes. Subdivide all polygonal segments at their box-boundary ports.
   Give the portions outside the boxes fresh distinct labels in their finite
   diagram-code order; designate the lexicographically smaller coordinate
   endpoint of each portion as its initial endpoint. Retain these portions,
   labels, and endpoints throughout that reduction tree. Inside each box record
   either the original crossing pairing or one of its two smoothing pairings;
   switches change only over/under data, and smoothings change only this pairing.
   In each current diagram, orient open strands from the smaller to the larger
   boundary endpoint label and order them by their initial endpoints. Order
   closed components by their least portion labels. Start each closed component
   along its least-labelled portion from its designated initial endpoint to its
   other endpoint, then follow its unique continuation. Inside a crossing box
   follow its current pairing. No portion is split or relabelled by a switch or
   smoothing, and every resulting component contains a labelled portion. This
   determines the traversal even when the designated directions of successive
   portions disagree.

cases.reason: The code labels label original polygonal segments, not the multiple pieces left when a smoothing deletes a crossing neighborhood. One segment can cross other segments more than once and its fragments can acquire different continuations/components. Retaining its old label and endpoints does not select a unique start piece or direction. The asserted deterministic procedure therefore lacks required instructions; procedure-properties Proof 1.2 explicitly relies on that missing choice. This does not refute the skein value or justify narrowing the algorithm/output.
cases.mathematical_check: Finite generic polygonal crossings admit such rational boxes. The retained outside portions connect box ports and original vertices/endpoints. Replacing a box pairing cannot create a component wholly inside one box, so every child component has a unique least-labelled portion. Switching preserves all connectivity and traversal, lowering bad-crossing count by exactly one. Smoothing can change traversal but reduces crossing count; the existing lexicographic termination proof and all three skein terms remain valid. No new prerequisite is required.

cases.original_concern: The Statement begins, 'Let K be a nonempty oriented link with determinant writhe w(K)'. Writhe and the regular-isotopy value D require a chosen diagram, whereas Q and F are ambient invariants. The intended identity is correct for each chosen diagram representing K, but that diagram choice should be explicit in this statement.

proposals.source_excerpt: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a nonempty oriented link with determinant writhe $w(K)$ and component count $c(K)$, and let $Q_K$ be the value returned by the BMW braid-closure algorithm for any finite signed braid word representing $K$.
proposals.proposed_replacement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix any nonempty oriented regular link diagram $K$, with determinant writhe $w(K)$ and component count $c(K)$. Let $Q_K$ denote the value returned by the BMW braid-closure algorithm for any finite signed braid word whose closure represents the oriented link represented by $K$. The quantities $D_K$ and $L_K$ below are evaluated on this fixed diagram; $F_K$ and $Q_K$ depend only on its ambient oriented link type.
